_provenance.notes: Alaska's cold, high-latitude waters are among the world's most vulnerable to ocean acidification (OA). Cold seawater absorbs CO2 more readily than tropical waters, and upwelling along the GOA and Bering Sea shelves brings naturally CO2-rich deep water to the surface. Surface ocean pH in the GOA has declined from ~8.10 in 1980 to ~8.01 in 2024 — a 22% increase in ocean acidity. Pteropods (sea butterflies), key prey for juvenile pink salmon and pollock, show shell dissolution at pH levels now commonly observed in GOA surface waters.

vulnerable_species.vulnerability: CRITICAL — shell dissolution at pH < 8.05, key juvenile salmon prey
HIGH — larvae die at aragonite saturation < 1.0
LOW-MODERATE — impacts on prey food web
